They had a median $884 per square foot, a median year built of 2020 and a median strata fee of $472 a month.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: streets and boundaries

items.t: Brentwood Park condos sit inside the Brentwood Town Centre in north Burnaby, one of four designated Town Centres in Burnaby's Official Community Plan, governed locally by the Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan adopted in 1996.

The plan area's core corner is Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue: the City states the Brentwood Site, the primary core of the plan area, is at the northeast corner of Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue, and the Buchanan West part of the centre is generally bounded by Lougheed Highway, Gilmore Avenue, Halifax Street and Madison Avenue/Douglas Street.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: the housing stock

items.t: The Brentwood condo stock is high-rise towers over a retail core, not low-rise walk-ups: the City's Burnaby 2050 policy guide states residential development in the Brentwood Town Centre is primarily apartments ranging from high-rise to mid-rise towers.

The Amazing Brentwood by SHAPE Properties is the anchor project at 4567 Lougheed Highway: SHAPE states it is a 28-acre site with more than 6,000 homes at completion over 11 residential towers, that Neighbourhood One is complete, and that Tower Six, with 369 homes, is the current tower selling in Neighbourhood Two.

Not every Amazing Brentwood tower is a condo: SHAPE states Tower One's 300 homes are professionally managed rental homes with full-time concierge, so a Brentwood buyer must separate the strata towers from the rental tower in the same project.

Concord Brentwood by Concord Pacific is the second master-planned cluster, on the south side of Lougheed Highway: its Hillside West homeowner page gives the addresses 4720 Lougheed Highway and 4730 Lougheed Highway, Burnaby, for its two towers.

Concord's next phase is Hillside East: Concord Pacific describes Hillside East as two elevated towers perched above the treetops, steps from SkyTrain and the Brentwood mall, as the newest phase of Concord Brentwood.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Brentwood Site Conceptual Master Plan, adopted in 2013, is the document that governs the Amazing Brentwood lands: the City states it outlines the principles guiding redevelopment of the site into a commercial and residential hub, and that the Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan is the community plan over it.

The plan is being amended for rentals and childcare: the City states recent changes to its Rental Use Zoning Policy and Child Care Action Plan provided the opportunity to revisit the Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan and the Brentwood Site Master Plan to provide more diverse housing options and social amenities.

One Amazing Brentwood parcel is proposed to change use: the City consultation describes redesignating the parcel at Willingdon Avenue and Lougheed Highway from commercial zoning to a mixed-use residential and commercial zoned site under the amended master plan.

A strata in Brentwood cannot ban long-term rentals: the Province states that as of November 24, 2022 no strata corporation is allowed to have a residential rental-restriction bylaw, while short-term rental restrictions still apply and a strata can fine up to $1,000 a day for breaching a short-term rental bylaw.

Age bylaws in a Brentwood strata are limited the same way: the Province states the only permitted strata age restriction is a 55-and-over bylaw kept to preserve seniors' housing, and an age bylaw setting a minimum below 55 is invalid.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The station above the condos was rebuilt while the towers rose: TransLink states the Brentwood Town Centre Station upgrades, completed for customers on March 24, 2025, added a new street-level elevator, two new escalators, an expanded mezzanine, three new fare gates and two glass-enclosed stairwells, a $32 million project.

Brentwood's new elementary school is a held site, not a built school: the City states the site at 4900 Dawson Street coincides with planned park and road works including the Dawson Street extension, and the school district still had to work through the steps to secure the site and request provincial capital funding.

Concord Brentwood units were built with building-wide water softening and electric vehicle charging at every residential parking stall: Concord Pacific states all buildings at Concord Brentwood incorporate a water softening system and all residential parking stalls have pre-installed 208 volt, 40 amp EV charging outlets.

The mall under the towers is a working construction site in phases: the City held its April 2, 2024 open house on the plan amendments inside The Amazing Brentwood at 4567 Lougheed Highway, second floor Centre Court — the project is still amending its master plan while people live in its first towers.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: development and new projects

items.t: Neighbourhood One is complete.

Concord Brentwood, Hillside East — Concord Pacific, two elevated towers in the Concord Brentwood community south of Lougheed Highway; status: described by the developer as the newest phase, coming soon on its project page (as of November 3, 2026).

New elementary school site, 4900 Dawson Street — City of Burnaby and Burnaby School District; status: site identified and held, funding request to the Ministry of Education and Child Care still to be advanced (as of November 3, 2026).

Brentwood Town Centre Plan Amendments — City of Burnaby amendments to the 1996 Development Plan and the 2013 Brentwood Site Master Plan for rental housing, childcare and the Willingdon/Lougheed parcel redesignation; status: consultation authorized January 29, 2024, project active (as of November 3, 2026).

2209 and 2225 Springer Avenue — proposed single high-rise apartment tower of up to 49 storeys with a nine-storey terraced podium and street-fronting retail, at the Brentwood plan edge; status: rezoning bylaw for first and second reading at Council on March 24, 2026, City public notice (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: costs and taxes

items.t: Burnaby's total 2026 residential property tax rate is $2.97749 per $1,000 of assessed value on the City's tax information page, made up of a $1.55649 City portion plus school at $1.01300, TransLink at $0.31410, Metro Vancouver at $0.05800 and BC Assessment at $0.03570.

Utility movement for a Brentwood condo in 2026 is stated by the City: water services increase 0 percent and sewer services increase 3.5 percent, approximately $14 for a condo, under the approved 2026–2030 Financial Plan with its 2.9 percent property tax increase.
Burnaby's rates bylaw for 2026 is Burnaby Rates Bylaw 2026, Bylaw No. 14814, adopted May 12, 2026 — the bylaw to cite when a strata's tax figure is questioned.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: getting around

items.t: Brentwood Town Centre Station on the Millennium Line is the centre's transit anchor: TransLink states it is a transfer point for seven bus routes — 25, 123, 130, 134, 136, 222 and N9 — connecting to UBC, New Westminster, Metrotown, North Vancouver, Coquitlam and late-night service from downtown Vancouver.

The station is the only SkyTrain station built on a roadway median, sitting in the middle of Lougheed Highway east of Willingdon Avenue, with a publicly accessible mezzanine that also works as a pedestrian crossing of the highway.

A future Metrotown–North Shore Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) line is planned through the station: TransLink states the BRT will operate between Metrotown and Park Royal via the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge, with Brentwood Town Centre Station one of the connection points used to set station locations.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check which master-plan phase a tower sits in before relying on a view or amenity: the Brentwood Site Master Plan is under amendment, including a proposed redesignation of the Willingdon Avenue and Lougheed Highway parcel from commercial to mixed-use residential and commercial, so land beside a finished tower can still change use.

Check tenure tower by tower in mixed projects: at The Amazing Brentwood the developer states Tower One is rental housing it manages itself, so a resale unit's neighbours and the building's strata documents differ from a pure strata tower — confirm the strata plan and tenure for the specific tower.

The railway is an active corridor through the plan area: the City's overpass study exists because the tracks are a barrier residents must cross, and condo units facing the corridor on Dawson Street and Willingdon Avenue should be checked for rail noise at viewing, a matter no City page quantifies.
